evals.prompt: Build out CODE_StockNewsPuller from plans/stock-news-puller-PRD.md. Keep going until the tests pass.
evals.expected_output: Enters a worktree, reads the PRD, establishes a test command, writes a task plan whose entries each cite a PRD section, runs buildloop.py init, then loops build/test/fix dispatching one subagent per task. Stops before merging and asks.
assertions: Creates a git worktree before writing code
Runs the existing test suite once before dispatching any build agent
Every task in the plan JSON has a non-empty acceptance string naming a runnable check
Runs the full test command itself after subagents return, not only the agents' own reports
Does not merge to master or push without asking

evals.prompt: implement the whole thing in CODE_PingWidget for me, spin up agents per task and dont stop to ask me every time something breaks
evals.expected_output: No PRD exists, so it writes a short spec to .buildloop/spec.md from the request, shows it, and proceeds. Iterates on failures without asking, up to 5 attempts per task, then stops.
assertions: Writes a spec file rather than blocking on the absence of a PRD
Does not ask the user after an individual test failure
Stops and reports when a task reaches 5 failed attempts
Commits each passing task separately on the worktree branch

evals.prompt: Run the build loop on CODE_Youtube_Rater — it has no tests directory at all.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes there is no verification gate, makes creating one the first task in the plan (add pytest to the manifest, create tests/), and only then builds features against it.
assertions: Task T1 establishes the test runner rather than implementing a feature
--test-command passed to init is a command that exists after T1 lands
Does not declare the build complete on a project where the test command was never run successfully

evals.prompt: The build loop on CODE_Thing stopped with T4 blocked after 5 tries. What now?
evals.expected_output: Reads state with `status`, reports T4's last_failure and what was attempted, and asks how to proceed. Does not silently start a sixth attempt or re-init the run.
assertions: Does not retry the blocked task without the user saying so
Does not run `init --force`, which would discard attempt history

take this spec and turn it into working tested code

check every 5 minutes whether the build finished
review this project and tell me what I should improve
